headline: Law adds about 9,290 acres to Nevada's Sloan Canyon National Conservation Area and grants land for a Southern Nevada water pipeline.
what_it_does: The law expands the Sloan Canyon National Conservation Area in Clark County, Nevada, by about 9,290 acres. It requires the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to give the Southern Nevada Water Authority rights-of-way to study the ground and to build and run a water pipeline through the area and other BLM land. The pipeline cannot go through or under wilderness areas and cannot permanently harm surface resources in the conservation area. The water authority may dig out and dispose of sand, gravel, and other materials while tunneling, on federal land chosen through an agreement with the BLM.

who_it_affects.how: It gets rights-of-way on federal land to investigate, build, and operate a water pipeline, subject to BLM conditions.
It must grant the rights-of-way, may set reasonable conditions to protect the area, and must sign an agreement on where dug-up materials can be disposed of.

who_it_affects.group: Utility companies with rights-of-way in the area
who_it_affects.how: Their existing rights and activities are protected, and the BLM can still approve new utility rights-of-way in the expanded area.

who_it_affects.group: Residents and visitors in Clark County, Nevada
who_it_affects.how: More land comes under conservation area protection, and a new water pipeline will be built through the region.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 19, 2026; no separate effective date is stated in the summary.
